pg-channel-diagnosis
Channel Diagnosis
[CHANNEL CONTEXT], [GOAL], [RECENT UPLOADS], [AVAILABLE ANALYTICS], [PRODUCTION CAPACITY]
Declare whether success means reach, qualified buyers, relationship or another concrete action. Do not silently substitute views for revenue.
Check watchability first: inspect supplied audio/video evidence or mark untested. Separate market ceiling, idea ceiling and execution capture; name the best-supported bottleneck.
Estimate the core floor from comparable ordinary uploads, with uncertainty. Separate it from potential new audience.
Choose one stage-appropriate intervention from the pendulum: basic quality, ideas/packaging, then higher production. Give a rejected alternative and the evidence that would reverse the choice.
One diagnosis with goal, observed evidence, three-ceiling map, pendulum stage, one intervention and validation test.

Goal: [outcome]
Evidence: [facts and missing inputs]
Bottleneck: [chosen cause and alternatives]
Intervention: [changed artifact]
Test: [measure and stop condition]
pg-ccn-slate
CCN Audience and Slate
[AUDIENCE], [CHANNEL PROMISE], [IDEA CANDIDATES], [RECENT TOPICS]
Describe core, casual and new by viewing familiarity. Keep buyer qualification as a separate dimension. A new viewer can still be an expert buyer.
For each candidate write the reason each group would click and stay. Find missing prerequisite knowledge and weave necessary context into action.
Compare neighboring topics through shared viewer motives. Treat the 80% overlap rule as a qualitative heuristic unless actual audience data exists.
Produce a coherent slate with a named experimental slot and a reason for each deliberate narrow business-purpose upload. Reject unrelated reach bait.
A slate table with CCN reasons, through-line, context repair, experiment status, goal and rejects.

Audience: [core / casual / new]
Through-line: [shared reason to return]
Slate: [idea | CCN reasons | continuity | goal]
Rejects: [idea and why]
Uncertainty: [unmeasured overlap]
pg-reference-analysis
Outlier Reference Analysis
[REFERENCE URLS OR EVIDENCE PACKAGES], [BASELINE UPLOADS], [TARGET AUDIENCE], [OWN ACCESS]
Reuse saved source evidence before any new video call. New paid analysis requires explicit batch approval and an enforceable budget; the trial grant is not reusable permission.
Calculate views relative to comparable creator history when supplied. Paddy uses approximately 3x as a research signal; absent baseline means candidate, not verified winner.
Compare outlier and ordinary neighboring uploads: topic, title, thumbnail situation, audience, access and release context. Separate visible observations, spoken claims and inferred causes.
Extract component mechanisms and assess Following / Strategy / Niche / Creator transfer with the existing Briar workflow when needed. Produce an original twist and list what cannot be borrowed.
A reference dossier with baseline math or missing-data flag, evidence timestamps, rival explanations, transfer verdict and original concept.

pg-idea-funnel
100 to 10 to 1 Idea Funnel
[GOAL], [AUDIENCE THROUGH-LINE], [REFERENCE BANK], [BUDGET AND ACCESS], [VIEW BASELINE]
Build a diverse raw pool from internal wins, external signals and explicitly labeled innovation. Use local reasoning; never create a paid loop to fill a quota.
For a full production decision, aim for 100 distinct premises. If evidence or scope supports fewer, show the actual count and call it a reduced run; never label 12 as 100.
Define roughly four or five elimination criteria: audience fit, clear packaging, feasibility, credible outcome potential and project-specific constraint. Calibrate overly loose or strict filters.

Develop ten survivors as one-page concepts: title options, rough thumbnail composition, logline, body skeleton, source hypothesis and cost/access needs. Reduced runs preserve the decision sequence with disclosed counts.
Choose one bet with a concrete reason and a falsification test. Declare expected performance as a hypothesis; do not invent historical support.
Raw idea pool, elimination ledger, finalist concept cards and one selected production bet with counts.

pg-title-lab
Title Lab
[SELECTED PREMISE], [FACTS AND PROOF], [AUDIENCE LANGUAGE], [THUMBNAIL CONCEPT]
Write at least ten genuinely different titles using story, comparison, consequence or a truthful contradiction. Do not merely change adjectives.
Use familiar words appropriate to the target audience. Preserve necessary specialist language when qualification is the goal. Read at a glance; avoid three competing mini-titles.
Pair titles with the thumbnail so each contributes information. Cut repetition unless it aids comprehension.
Choose one title and explain its open question and promised payoff. Treat brevity as a tool, not a hard 50-character rule. Reject any superlative or number lacking evidence.
Ten titles, paired thumbnail role, one selected title, rejected misleading options and payoff check.

Selected: [title]
Thumbnail contributes: [new information]
Open question: [question]
Payoff evidence: [proof]
Rejected: [unsupported claims]
pg-thumbnail-concepts
Thumbnail Concept Briefs
[LOCKED TITLE], [ACTUAL VIDEO], [AVAILABLE PEOPLE AND ASSETS], [BRAND CUES]
Define the unresolved action or thought that the click starts. Use click-to-unpause only where the actual content supports that situation.
Design three conceptually distinct compositions: different visual explanations of the premise, not cosmetic shirt-color variants.
For each specify subject, action, hierarchy, framing, crop, optional minimal text, truthful evidence and the title’s complementary role. Remove elements that compete with the central question.
Preserve necessary recognition cues for an established channel. Flag missing source shots and hand a brief to the existing visual craft owner; never pretend a prose brief is a rendered image.
Three visual briefs with composition, evidence, capture needs and a glance-test checklist.

pg-packaging-capture
Packaging Capture Plan
[SELECTED IDEA], [TEN TITLES], [THREE CONCEPT BRIEFS], [SHOOT CONSTRAINTS]
Choose a provisional title before committing to production. Translate each thumbnail concept into images that must exist after the shoot.
Write shot requirements: location, person/object, angle, microexpression, action moment, lighting and crop-safe space. Allow several variants per concept, scaled to the actual production budget.
Check feasibility before filming: access, props, whether the image misrepresents events, and whether every promised outcome can be delivered.
Output a capture checklist and handoff for three finished designs. Do not require 50 paid designs simply because a large client once used them.
A shoot-ready thumbnail capture checklist and design handoff, tied to three concepts.

pg-intro-rewrite
Promise-First Intro
[TITLE AND THUMBNAIL PROMISE], [SOURCE SCRIPT OR FACTS], [FIRST BODY BEAT], [FORMAT]
Identify the exact expectation created by the package. In the first seconds confirm it verbally or visually using available proof.
Open a small set of answerable questions. Replace a list of agenda statements with interest in outcomes; defer biography and unnecessary setup.
Write a connecting line that begins the first substantive beat without an intro-ending reset. Seed any relationship a new viewer needs inside the action.
Normally keep the intro under 45 seconds; estimate duration from spoken length. A montage or longer setup needs a format-specific reason. Include a promise-to-payoff map for the editor.
One finished intro with visual cues, estimated duration, first body transition and promise/payoff map.

Transition: [first body beat]

pg-stakes-design
Audience-Relevant Stakes
[PREMISE], [AUDIENCE], [REAL CONSEQUENCES], [AVAILABLE PROOF]
Name why this viewer should care before selecting a storytelling structure. Distinguish curiosity about outcome from relevance of outcome.
Generate alternatives using genuine opposition, time, reward, uncertainty or cost of ignorance. Label hypothetical consequences as hypothetical.
Reject consequences that belong to the performer rather than the viewer’s reason for watching; apply the source’s investment/slime anti-example.
Write the strongest stakes line and integrate it into a brief scene or explanation. Do not invent money losses, danger, humiliation or fabricated antagonists.
Three stakes candidates, rejected mismatch, selected finished passage and proof requirements.

Reject: [mismatch and why]

Proof: [what supports the consequence]
pg-launch-experiment
Launch Expectations and Test Plan
[SELECTED TITLE], [THREE THUMBNAILS], [COMPARABLE UPLOADS], [BUSINESS GOAL]
Before publishing, record expected first-hour/day/week outcomes as ranges, their evidence and the purpose of the upload. Unknown baselines stay unknown.
Start with one chosen title and three genuinely different thumbnail concepts. Verify current platform test availability before any live action; this workflow does not publish.
Define when to inspect results and what magnitude/context would justify a change. A recent-video rank is evidence relative to history, not a substitute for expectations.
Keep a working package; when the current package underperforms credible expectations, make one reasoned change and record it. Flag insufficient samples, traffic changes and attribution limits.

pg-retention-diagnosis
Retention Diagnosis
[RETENTION CURVE OR EXPORT], [VIDEO OR TIMESTAMPED SCRIPT], [TRAFFIC CONTEXT], [PRIOR VERSION]
If no actual retention data exists, produce a script risk audit and label it clearly; never draw an invented curve.
Compare curve shape and departures with the video: promise failure, missing context, irrelevant stakes, conclusion language or slow reset. Distinguish observation from causal hypothesis.
Account for changing audience mix: a broader distribution can lower aggregate CTR and average retention while increasing views.
Choose one repair at an evidenced moment and write the replacement passage or edit instruction. Specify what a future comparison would need to test that hypothesis.

pg-platform-transfer
Long-Form to Short-Form Transfer
[SOURCE VIDEO EVIDENCE], [TARGET PLATFORM], [AUDIENCE], [ORIGINAL ANGLE]
Extract the long-form promise, audience motive, intrinsic stakes and necessary proof from timestamps. Separate these from thumbnail-click and long-intro mechanics.
For a served feed, convert the package promise into the opening visible/spoken moment; do not transplant a 45-second intro.
Load only the relevant existing Jenny Hoyos or Kallaway workflow for short-form execution after inspecting available skill paths. Give it the selected mechanism, not the entire expert corpus.
Produce an original short script and shot plan with a complete payoff, preserving factual boundaries. List what changed for platform and what remains untested.

Connected Creative Strategy Sprint
[PROJECT GOAL], [AUDIENCE], [SOURCE BANK], [PRODUCTION LIMITS], [KNOWN PERFORMANCE]
Paddy owns the strategy. Use Briar only to establish outlier/transfer evidence when that gap exists; preserve separate audience familiarity and commercial qualification.

Prepare pre-publish expectations and measurement plan. Route final metadata to the existing YouTube content-package skill only after the promise is locked.
Deliver one coherent production packet and proof gaps. Paid perception, image generation, publishing and batch expansion remain explicit decisions; no automatic calls from this workflow.

pg-learning-bank
Content Analyst Learning Bank
[ANALYZED REFERENCES], [USER TASTE VERDICTS IF ANY], [PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE], [NEXT CONTENT JOB]
Organize references by the problem they solve: idea, title, thumbnail, intro or retention. Store source URL and timestamps, evidence type and access/capture status.
Keep three separate assessments: measured performance, declared personal taste and inferred mechanism. Unknown taste is not learned preference.
Write a reusable move with trigger, action, counterexample, transfer limits and a pointer to the focused workflow. Deduplicate the same source and same analysis request before any retrieval.
Retrieve only the two or three references that change the next content decision; propose one original application. Do not schedule scans or turn the $10 trial into a standing allowance.
